vulnerabilities.description: glob 10.2.0-10.4.5: Command injection via -c/--cmd executes matches with shell:true (GHSA-5j98-mcp5-4vw2). Used indirectly via @next/eslint-plugin-next and eslint-config-next.

Next.js 9.3.4-16.3.0-canary.5: Multiple DoS and security vulnerabilities including HTTP request smuggling in rewrites (GHSA-ggv3-7p47-pfv8), Image Optimizer DoS (GHSA-9g9p-9gw9-jx7f), XSS in CSP nonces (GHSA-ffhc-5mcf-pf4q), and Server Components DoS (GHSA-q4gf-8mx6-v5v3).
PostCSS <8.5.10: XSS vulnerability via unescaped </style> in CSS stringify output (GHSA-qx2v-qp2m-jg93). Affects Next.js build process.

Memory JSON file created with world-readable permissions (rw-rw-r--). If containing sensitive configuration or credentials, any user on the system can read it. Use fs.writeFileSync with explicit mode 0o600.
Temporary file created without explicit file permissions (rw-rw-r--). Sensitive GitHub content passed via body parameter could be read by other users. Use fs.writeFileSync with mode 0o600 or mkdtemp.
Session ID generated using Date.now() which is predictable and not cryptographically random. An attacker could predict session IDs. Use crypto.randomBytes() instead.
Session JSON files created without explicit file permissions (rw-rw-r--). Session context could be read by other system users. Set mode 0o600 when writing.
JSON parsing errors silently caught and ignored without logging. Corrupted memory.json files fail silently, potentially losing state without alerting the user.
File operations on .swarm/security and .claude/security paths without path normalization. While unlikely to be exploited, use path.resolve() for defense in depth against directory traversal.

recommendations: CRITICAL: Update Next.js to 16.2.6+ to fix DoS vulnerabilities, XSS flaws, and HTTP request smuggling
CRITICAL: Update glob to 10.5.0+ or skip ESLint glob plugin usage to prevent command injection
CRITICAL: Update PostCSS to 8.5.10+ to fix XSS in CSS stringify
Run 'npm audit fix --force' and thoroughly test the application after upgrading dependencies
Fix file permission issues in helper scripts: Use fs.writeFileSync(path, data, { mode: 0o600 }) for all sensitive files
Replace Date.now() session ID generation with crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('hex') for cryptographic security
Add console.error() logging in memory.js JSON parsing to catch and report file corruption
Consider encrypting sensitive stored data using crypto.createCipheriv() if credentials will be persisted
Run 'npm audit' regularly and set up automated vulnerability scanning in CI/CD
Review and restrict file permissions on all data directories (memory, sessions, security scans)
